name: Flame Organ
description: A small flame in a glass tube for every key: it flutters, catches, makes the whole tube sing, and can lift the note to another of the tube's harmonics or beat against a second flame.

params.name: Flame
params.description: How tall the flame burns. A small one sings almost a pure tone; a tall one beats the air in hard pulses, with every harmonic of the tube.

params.name: Lag
params.description: How late the flame answers the air, as a share of the note's period. It chooses the harmonic that sings and how the others stand around it.

params.name: Place
params.description: How high in the tube the flame stands. Each harmonic is fed or starved by where the flame is, so the colour moves from bright and thin to hollow.

params.name: Tube
params.description: The tube that sings: all harmonics, the odd ones, a bright horn, a thin flute, or two pipes with one an octave below.

params.name: Fuel
params.description: What burns. Gas is steady and warm, a candle soft and fluttering, spirit hard and clear, coal rough and dark with a crackle.

params.name: Second Flame
params.description: Lights a second tube beside the first, with its flame at another place. Between says how the two get on.

params.name: Between
params.description: How far apart the two flames stand. Close, they lock into one tone; further off they slip and pull; at the end each beats freely against the other.

params.name: Flicker
params.description: How unsteadily each flame burns. Much of it makes the note gutter, sink to a thread and take hold again, each key in its own time.

params.name: Catch
params.description: How long the tube takes to catch. Short speaks like a struck key; long flutters and breathes before the tone swells out of it.

params.name: Burn
params.description: How long a held flame has fuel for. It thins and dies by itself after this time; at the top it burns for as long as the key is held.

params.name: Embers
params.description: How long the tube goes on after the key is let go, growing purer as the flame sinks.

params.name: Roar
params.description: How much the burning itself is heard: turbulence that breathes in the tube and a rush of air around it, in the colour of the fuel.

params.name: Draught
params.description: A slow current of air through all the tubes at once. It leans on every flame, so colour and strength move together like weather.

params.name: Lift
params.description: How readily a note leaves its first harmonic for the next one of the tube. Some lift now and then by themselves; at the top all live up there.

params.name: Glass
params.description: The glass of the tube, tapped as the flame is lit. More of it rings louder and longer, and then hums faintly along with the tube.

params.name: Mouth
params.description: How far the mouth of the tubes is open. Covered it is dark and near; open it lets out the upper harmonics and the air.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far apart harmonics and flames stand between the speakers. At zero everything is in the middle.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. The modes of a tube driven by a heat release that answers the tube's own air late are the textbook thermoacoustic ones; the flame's answer is a smooth saturation made here, the lag is a turn of each mode's phase, and every level is set by measurement.
